youtube.title: TECH TUESDAY
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Steven Sykes work through a backlog of listener questions on Tech Tuesday, covering EMF exposure from Starlink dishes, the trade-offs between budget de-Googled phones and Google Pixels running GrapheneOS and how to keep banking apps isolated on a de-Googled device. Steven also recounts a chaotic trailer hire gone wrong thanks to a QR-code booking system, before they turn to concerns about data collection in Chinese-made EVs and the rise of drone-delivered battlefield robots in Ukraine. Cut through the hype. Get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: THE WILMS REPORT
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by Tim Wilms for a wide-ranging look at the past fortnight in Australia — kicking off with the AFL Grand Final before turning to Albanese’s global AI push, falling poll numbers, rising fuel prices, migration and Australia’s ageing population. They also discuss the OpenAI Medicare data incident, the media’s focus on One Nation and the passing of Australian rock legend Angry Anderson. NOTE: A 2022 review ( https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10087409/ ) found 10 of 12 peer-reviewed studies reported statistically significant increases in domestic violence, while Australian research and police data ( https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-09-27/domestic-violence-spike-major-sport-events-afl-nrl-rugby-footy/104399938 ) found similar increases — including almost 40% higher victimisation on State of Origin nights and a 20% rise in Victoria Police call-outs around the AFL Grand Final. Discover more from Tim at The Unshackled

youtube.title: DRS SARAH AND RANDALL FARRANT
youtube.summary: Rodney Hide is joined by Drs Sarah and Randall Farrant to explore the “anatomy of a cold” and challenge the way we think and talk about illness. They examine the idea of a cold as a “health expression”, the influence of language and beliefs and the events and experiences that may precede physical symptoms, encouraging a different perspective on health and wellbeing. For more information: Check out the Vital Wellbeing website , the Vital Wellbeing blog and Vital Wellbeing shop Follow Vital Wellbeing on Facebook , Instagram and Rumble

youtube.title: WINSTON PETERS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan continues his weekly pre-election chat with NZ First leader and Foreign Minister Winston Peters, covering plans to abolish the Waitangi Tribunal, a proposed tax rate cut for small businesses, organic farming policy, John Key's overhang comments and shifting poll numbers. Winston also responds to a Tauranga meeting attendee's account of vaccine injury, calling for a fuller inquiry. Discover more from Winston Peters on X , Facebook and Instagram For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: DANIEL BURGESS
youtube.summary: Natalie Cutler-Welsh speaks with men's mentor and coach Daniel Burgess about his path from a near-fatal accident and homelessness to helping men build emotional intelligence and purpose. Daniel explains why men typically need a concrete reason, not abstract self-improvement, to begin inner work and the pair explore healing childhood wounds, the stories we build around our past and the shifting balance between masculine and feminine energy in relationships. Discover more from Daniel on Facebook and at DanielAI For more from Natalie check out UpyourBrave

youtube.title: BEN DUXSON
youtube.summary: Michael Arbon speaks with sixth-generation farmer Ben Duxson about the community resistance to Victoria's VNI West transmission project, which would run through prime agricultural land near his property. Ben details the fines issued to farmers who blocked survey access, the pressure tactics used by VicGrid and the grassroots Farmers Fight Back movement now pushing back through direct lobbying. For more information visit Farmers Fightback on Facebook Discover more from Michael on Facebook and X

youtube.title: BRENDAN HOARE
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan speaks with Brendan Hoare, spokesperson for Organics Aotearoa New Zealand, about the organisation’s new political scorecard assessing party support for the organic sector. They examine the seven policy areas, where parties have committed—or fallen short—and the sector’s push for stronger government recognition, export opportunities and protection of New Zealand’s GE-free advantage. For more from OANZ or check out their OANZ Vote Organic 2026 Election Manifesto Listen to Brendan's last interview on RCR | Organic sector calls for investment ahead of election For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: JULIA RUCKLIDGE
youtube.summary: Host Maree Buscke talks with Professor Julia Rucklidge (University of Canterbury psychologist and co-author of The Better Brain) about NZ First's newly announced “Make New Zealand Healthy” policy. Julia describes feeling validated by the policy, noting it echoes ideas she and colleagues (Glenn Davis, Tim Muir, Grant Schofield) have advocated for years around shifting from a reactive “sick-care” system to preventative health. For more from Julia, check out her University of Canterbury webpage or find her on Facebook and X Catch Julia's previous interview with Maree on 21st August | Micronutrients for mental health in pregnancy – the evidence For news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday
